title: After the loans, the contracts remain: China’s new Balkan model
gist: Chinese infrastructure loans to the Western Balkans have largely disappeared, but Chinese state-owned contractors have stayed, winning 22 projects between July 2021 and July 2026 without disclosed Chinese loan financing, often funded by EU/EBRD money or local budgets. Montenegro's EBRD/EU-funded second Bar–Boljare highway section, won by a POWERCHINA-led consortium for about EUR 694m, epitomizes a model where Europe finances and Chinese SOEs build.

themes.theme: From loan packages to contractor model

insights.claim: China's former Western Balkans model bundled an Export-Import Bank of China loan, sovereign debt for the host government, and a construction contract for a Chinese state-owned enterprise, often via bilateral agreements rather than open procurement.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Explains the legacy of sovereign debt exposures to China in the region.
insights.locator: For much of the previous decade

insights.claim: Large new Chinese loans have all but disappeared from the Western Balkans infrastructure pipeline as China's overseas development lending remains far below its 2015–2017 peak and the EU, EBRD, EIB and domestic budgets have expanded their role.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: European development finance is now the main funding source for Balkan infrastructure.
insights.quote: Large new Chinese loans have now all but disappeared from the regional infrastructure pipeline.
insights.locator: Large new Chinese loans

insights.claim: Research identified 22 Western Balkan projects awarded to Chinese implementing companies between July 2021 and July 2026 without disclosed Chinese loan financing: 16 in Serbia, three in Bosnia and Herzegovina, two in Montenegro and one in Albania.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Chinese SOE contractors remain entrenched even as Chinese lending recedes.
insights.locator: Yet the retreat of Chinese lending

insights.claim: Of the 22 Chinese-implemented Western Balkan projects, 14 rely mainly on public budgets or domestic bank borrowing, five on EBRD loans, EU grants or related European financing, and three on private investment, concessions or project finance.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Chinese contractors now earn revenue from local and European money rather than Chinese credit.
insights.locator: Fourteen of the 22 projects

insights.claim: University of Belgrade's Nenad Stekić says Beijing has become more selective with sovereign loans due to pressures on China's domestic financial system, limited profitability of some Belt and Road projects, and a desire to reduce political and credit risk abroad.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Signals continued retrenchment of Chinese policy-bank overseas lending.
insights.quote: Beijing has become considerably more selective in approving sovereign loans due to pressures on China’s domestic financial system
insights.locator: For Nenad Stekić, assistant professor

insights.claim: The article argues that China no longer needs to be the Western Balkans' lender of first resort to preserve its infrastructure position, and that the contractor-led model is more mature and potentially more durable.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Declining Chinese lending should not be read as declining Chinese commercial footprint in Europe's periphery.
insights.quote: This is a more mature and potentially more durable form of engagement.
insights.locator: China no longer needs to act

insights.claim: Montenegro borrowed USD 944 million from the Export-Import Bank of China in 2014 for the first 41-km Bar–Boljare highway section built by CRBC, and when repayments began in 2021 it needed hedging deals with Western banks to manage currency exposure and lower the effective rate.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: The region's archetypal case of dollar-denominated Chinese debt creating fiscal and FX stress.
insights.locator: Montenegro’s second highway test

insights.claim: The second Bar–Boljare section (Mateševo–Andrijevica, about 22 km) is financed by a EUR 200 million EBRD loan, a EUR 150 million EU grant and Montenegro's budget, and was won by a POWERCHINA, STECOL and POWERCHINA Chengdu consortium bidding about EUR 694 million before VAT.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Concrete example of Chinese SOEs capturing EU-funded construction revenue.
insights.locator: The second section has an almost reversed

insights.claim: In the Montenegro highway tender, China Communications Construction Company also submitted a qualified financial offer and the only non-Chinese qualified bidder was the Cengiz-Azvirt consortium, so Chinese firms dominated the final field despite European financing.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Shows how thin European contractor participation is in Balkan infrastructure tenders.
insights.quote: European money therefore supported a tender in which Chinese companies dominated the final field.
insights.locator: The field itself revealed the construction strength

insights.claim: Mladen Grgić says Montenegro does not seek Chinese loans because Western and European financing is available and Chinese loans are politically costly for a country fully aligned with EU foreign policy and on the verge of EU accession.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: EU accession prospects effectively crowd out Chinese sovereign lending in candidate countries.
insights.quote: Montenegro is not seeking financing from China because funding is available from Western and European banks
insights.locator: For Mladen Grgić, teaching associate

insights.claim: The article argues that when Chinese state-owned companies win EU- or EBRD-funded tenders, Europe finances infrastructure while part of the long-term commercial benefit, experience and local influence flows to its principal systemic competitor.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Could prompt EU moves to tighten procurement rules against state-subsidized bidders, affecting Chinese contractors' European pipeline.
insights.quote: Europe finances infrastructure while part of the long-term commercial benefit flows to its principal systemic competitor.
insights.locator: European institutions mobilize public money

insights.claim: Croatia's Pelješac Bridge, 85% funded by EU cohesion funds and built by CRBC after a competitive tender, is the key precedent of Chinese SOEs undercutting European competitors under EU rules and turning the result into a commercial reference.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Demonstrates Chinese contractors can win flagship EU-funded projects inside the bloc.
insights.locator: The Western Balkans did not create this dilemma

insights.claim: Grgić argues European construction companies are often smaller, fragmented and more expensive, while former loan-for-investment Chinese firms have become competitive even under EBRD procurement standards.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: European construction firms face structural cost disadvantages versus Chinese SOEs in open tenders.
insights.quote: The EU has created a framework in which European companies are often smaller, fragmented, and more expensive.
insights.locator: Grgić sees Montenegro’s second highway section

insights.claim: Chinese firms have also won EBRD-supported projects including Sarajevo's tram track reconstruction, Montenegro's Tivat–Jaz road, and Albania's Vau i Dejës floating solar project, implemented by a Sungrow-Gamma Solutions consortium.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Chinese participation extends into renewables and urban transport, not just highways.
insights.locator: The pattern now appears across the Western Balkans

insights.claim: The author proposes that Western Balkan tenders require transparent ownership information, disclosure of state support, realistic assessment of abnormally low bids, and stronger monitoring of subcontracting, labor, environmental and lifecycle costs, rather than nationality-based exclusion.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Signals the likely direction of procurement reform affecting Chinese SOE contractors in Europe.
insights.locator: The relevant policy question

insights.claim: The article notes that if European contractors avoid complex Western Balkan projects, Chinese companies will not need political favoritism to expand.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Market share in Balkan infrastructure is partly a function of European contractors' own risk appetite.
insights.quote: Governments cannot award contracts to companies that do not bid
insights.locator: European firms also need to decide

insights.claim: Serbia accounts for 16 of the 22 identified Chinese-implemented projects without Chinese loans, most funded by the Serbian budget or domestic borrowing, with some awarded via direct agreements under Serbia's intergovernmental framework with China.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Serbia is China's main construction platform in the region and a mixed competitive/political access model.
insights.locator: Serbia and the politics of access

insights.claim: POWERCHINA is building Serbia's Expo 2027 complex in Surčin and related infrastructure, funded by the Serbian budget (47.5 billion dinars allocated in 2026) and long-term government bonds rather than a Chinese loan.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Expo spending adds to Serbian public debt via bond issuance, relevant for Serbian sovereign credit.
insights.quote: The 2026 budget allocated 47.5 billion dinars to Expo preparations
insights.locator: Expo 2027 takes this approach

insights.claim: Serbia's special Expo law exempts key Surčin projects from the ordinary Law on Public Procurement, which Transparency Serbia argues removes legal protection for bidders and risks higher costs than genuine competition.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Opaque procurement raises cost-overrun and governance risk around Serbian public finances.
insights.locator: The special law adopted for Expo-related construction

insights.claim: Chinese companies do not win every contest: Azerbaijan's Azvirt took over parts of Serbia's 'Smile of Vojvodina' expressway after a framework deal with a Chinese state contractor broke down over construction pace and financing commitments.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Chinese commercial access in the Balkans is substantial but not absolute.
insights.quote: Chinese commercial access is substantial rather than absolute.
insights.locator: Yet Chinese companies do not win every contest
